answer: The protocol mandates 2,000 units of computational work per identity to bridge the entry gap, ensuring that while an honest agent pays this fixed base cost, an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must solve 2,000,000 units to bypass the gate. A verifier acts as a sturdy timber frame, rejecting any reused output or stale evidence to keep the registry pure. This mechanism assumes individual compute nodes cannot collude to share solutions. Like a plume of smoke rising from a unique fire, each identity is distinct. Every verified sonnet of code creates an immutable ledger entry.
